implementation_notes: Same runtime as JavaScript, plus a typed contract over the merged result: Promise.all with an as const tuple (or an explicit tuple type) makes the aggregate's shape part of the signature, and a discriminated union of partial messages makes the merge exhaustive in a switch. The classic collector is still needed for message-stream aggregation, because the type system provides no correlation or completeness: type the correlation id as a branded type and the store as Map<CorrelationId, PartialMessage[]> so a wrong key or partial cannot be stored silently.
pitfalls: Promise.all's inferred type is an array, not a tuple, unless the input is as const - the merged result loses per-element types until the tuple is annotated.
A typed partial-message union does not de-duplicate at runtime: retried messages still appear twice and TypeScript will not warn.
Result order is input order, not completion order, so a first-best condition needs a race/promise-with-timeout helper rather than Promise.all.

variants.name: RxJS forkJoin / combineLatest operator pipeline
variants.implementation_notes: Reactive realization: forkJoin(part$...) emits once when every inner Observable completes - literally the wait-for-all completeness condition - and combineLatest/zip cover the streaming cases where the aggregate updates on each arrival, while bufferTime/timeout implement the time-based conditions. Reach for it when the partials are already streams (websockets, Kafka clients, Angular HttpClient) or when retries, cancellation and back-pressure must be expressed as operators, because the operator tree replaces the hand-written collector; a plain Promise.all is simpler when there are no subscriptions to manage.
pitfalls: forkJoin emits nothing if any inner Observable completes without emitting: one empty partial silently kills the aggregate.
Without a timeout operator the subscription waits forever, and an incomplete aggregate leaks its subscription.
Subscriptions must be torn down (takeUntil/Subscription.unsubscribe); re-subscribing a hot source per aggregate duplicates partials.
